TYPE CHECK: The candidate value is a chemical reagent used for alkylation, which matches the field definition.
SOURCE CHECK: The value is reasonably inferable from the text; the paper explicitly mentions "20 mM IAA (indole-3-acetic acid) alkylation".
TRUTH CHECK: While the paper uses the abbreviation "IAA", it identifies it as "indole-3-acetic acid". In the context of proteomics alkylation, "IAA" almost always refers to iodoacetamide, but the authors explicitly wrote "indole-3-acetic acid", which is a plant hormone, not an alkylating agent. However, the process described is "alkylation", and "iodoacetamide" is the standard reagent for this step. The authors likely mislabeled the chemical name while using the correct abbreviation (IAA) and the correct process (alkylation).
COMPLETENESS CHECK: The full set contains the only alkylation reagent mentioned.
TYPE_CORRECT: yes
